title: NASA Aviation Safety Reporting System: confidential voluntary aviation incident reporting as a weak-signal commons
summary: ASRS is promoted as the cube’s first explicit weak-signal infrastructure record: a voluntary, confidential, non-punitive aviation reporting system that captures, de-identifies, analyzes, alerts, educates, and publishes sanitized data while carrying explicit scope limits.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0007 as a source-infrastructure record for the near-miss / signal-capture lane.

claims.claim: ASRS collects voluntarily submitted aviation incident/situation reports, acts on the information in them, identifies system deficiencies, issues alerting messages to people positioned to correct them, educates through publications, and maintains a public database for safety research and policy.
what_would_change_status: A later ASRS program page or FAA source changes the described functions.

claims.claim: ASRS reporting is voluntary; NASA states reports are held in strict confidence, de-identified before database entry, and that more than one million reports had been submitted with no ASRS reporter identity breach to date.
what_would_change_status: A later NASA disclosure, legal source, or program audit revises confidentiality history or submission count.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: FAA describes ASRS as a 1976 NASA/FAA partnership that is confidential, non-punitive, voluntary, and offers confidentiality plus limited enforcement immunity; FAA also describes ASRS outputs as Safety Alerts/FYI notices, CALLBACK, studies, and a public database.
what_would_change_status: FAA revises ASRS legal protections, partnership description, or program outputs.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: ASRS has explicit scope limits: protections do not extend to accidents or criminal activity; waiver conditions are limited; reports may be screened and forwarded identified in excluded categories, while normal processing returns ID strips and de-identifies records.
what_would_change_status: A newer Advisory Circular or statute changes reporting exclusions, de-identification practice, or waiver policy.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no outcome evaluation or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, and reported process; it does not estimate effectiveness, representativeness, underreporting, or downstream safety impact.
No reporter narratives are imported in rev0007; privacy and de-identification boundaries are preserved.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: United States National Airspace System, aviation participants and related UAS/HazMat reporting contexts as described by ASRS/FAA pages
reporter_protection_design: identity strip return / no retained identity copy except exclusions
limited FAA enforcement-use waiver subject to criteria
third-party NASA role separated from FAA enforcement
limitations: excludes accidents and criminal activity from protections
narratives are sanitized and not automatically representative
type_payload.query_value: Provides a model for converting near-misses, anomalies, and weak warnings into searchable, de-identified safety intelligence before catastrophe.

handling_notes: Do not attempt to re-identify reporters or named parties from confidential/de-identified reporting systems.
Infrastructure records are not evidence that all weak signals were handled well or that a reporting system prevented a specific accident.
Preserve distinction among mandatory reporting, voluntary self-reporting, confidential concern reporting, accident investigation, and recommendation tracking.

unknowns: Quantitative uptake, underreporting, signal quality, follow-through rates, and confidentiality failure history are not extracted yet.
No sample of individual reports, alerts, recommendations, or closed actions has been coded yet.
next_actions: Add database/export sampling plan and legal/ethical handling rules before importing any de-identified report narratives.
Add outcome or follow-through records showing when a report led to action, when it did not, and when confidentiality or reporting incentives failed.
Cross-link with warning-governance cases only when a source shows a specific relation; do not infer relation from infrastructure existence.
